input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md (sole technical authority; the single USER passage in input/conversation.md is a truncated verbatim subset of it and adds nothing) and input/brief.md (formalities only). I traced every limitation of all sixteen claims, every sentence of the field, summary, drawing list, detailed description and abstract, all twenty-five numerals, and all four figure briefs to exact affirmative disclosure passages. Independent claims 1 and 11 map element-for-element to "Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier", "A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors", "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus", the stored authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit set, the per-interval subtraction of "measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit", sustaining-first then deficit distribution, pilot send plus connector-sensor verification, and "If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit" (the reduced-command trigger and the re-measure-and-stop recitation of claims 2/12 follow from "one at a time ... until"). Dependent claims 3/13 (zero connector current, connected vehicle, randomized recovery delay), 4/14 (leakage threshold, inhibit other contactors, local fault indicator), 5 (isolated local bus), 6/15 (network interface, signed local token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation subject to the independent branch-current process), 7 (token authorizes that connector and has not expired), 8 (tamper-evident local sequence uploaded on return), and 9/10/16 (service input, one low-energy pilot transition at a time, store only after the sensed channel agrees) each rest on a quoted affirmative disclosure sentence. Description-only elaborations are definitional or direct corollaries (e.g. "opens no further contactor once ... below the branch current limit" from "until"; "the remaining connector channels still charging" from opening only as many as needed; the wiring-transposition rationale from "This prevents a wiring-map error from assigning a current limit to the wrong connector"); I found no untraced structure, material, operating condition, result, or optional embodiment. Figure briefs assert only disclosed parts and disclosed topology: branch conductor with the branch sensor in series and all loads tapped downstream (from "measures total current" plus "measured non-charging branch load"), contactor in series ahead of the connector current sensor and vehicle connector, pilot interface to the connector, bus to contactor and pilot interface only (not to the non-charging load, which the controller "does not command"), sensor sensing lines to the controller, and the FIG. 4 sequence matching steps 202-216 including the branch-current return path, the welded branch to a terminator, and the reclosure return path. Generic outlines (dashed installation boundary, square sensor, circle sensor, rounded vehicle, plain blocks, terminator square) are each called "shown schematically" or sit in a figure the brief and the Brief Description call schematic/block/flow, the claims and description stay shape-neutral, and no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or other shape-justifying or broadening language leaked into the application text. Internal consistency checks passed: claims and description use identical relationships and terms (branch current limit, last accepted branch limit, minimum sustaining current, energy-deficit value, stored shedding order, verification interval, randomized recovery delay, leakage threshold, low-energy pilot transition); each numeral denotes exactly one part and every numeral in the ledger appears in both a figure brief and the description with the same name; six rectangles plus two diamonds reconcile with the eight listed steps 202-216 and with the per-numeral leader list; FIG. 3's dashed branch-sensor line and solid bus and connector-sensor lines match FIG. 1 and FIG. 2; no sectional views exist, so no section-line designation is required; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains. Cross-reference and government-support sections correctly read "Not applicable" per the brief, and the abstract is 146 words with no means-plus-function language in any claim. No unsupported technical assertion or verified inconsistency was found.
